Input_or_Condition: A supported business intent is expressed clearly in German.
Required_Data: Customer request plus data required by the underlying use case.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; sources required by the underlying use case
Expected_Response_Behavior: Process the underlying use case normally and generate the draft in German.
Escalation_Condition: Use the escalation rule of the underlying use case.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not change the business logic because of language.
Acceptance_Criteria: The business outcome matches the underlying use case; response language is German; source and safety rules remain unchanged.

Input_or_Condition: A supported business intent is expressed clearly in English.
Required_Data: Customer request plus data required by the underlying use case.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; sources required by the underlying use case
Expected_Response_Behavior: Process the underlying use case normally and generate the draft in English.
Escalation_Condition: Use the escalation rule of the underlying use case.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not change the business logic because of language.
Acceptance_Criteria: The business outcome matches the equivalent German scenario; response language is English; source and safety rules remain unchanged.

Input_or_Condition: The customer's language cannot be determined reliably, but the business intent is sufficiently clear.
Required_Data: Customer request plus data required by the underlying use case.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; sources required by the underlying use case
Expected_Response_Behavior: Apply the underlying use-case logic and use German as the defined fallback language.
Escalation_Condition: Use the escalation rule of the underlying use case.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not classify the request as ambiguous solely because the language is uncertain when the intent is clear.
Acceptance_Criteria: German fallback is used; the underlying business decision is unchanged; no unsupported facts are added.

Input_or_Condition: The request is too vague or ambiguous to determine what the customer wants.
Required_Sources: Customer Request
Expected_Response_Behavior: Generate a concise clarification question instead of a substantive answer.
Clarification_Condition: Always when the intent cannot be determined reliably.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate if the intent remains unresolved after clarification or requires manual interpretation.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not guess a specific intent, order problem or policy outcome.
Acceptance_Criteria: No substantive business answer is generated; clarification is relevant to the ambiguity; no unsupported assumption is introduced.

Input_or_Condition: The intent is clear, but the topic is outside Shipping, Returns, Refund Policy and Order Status, for example account access or warranty.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Business Rules
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not answer the unsupported topic as if it were covered; route it to normal human handling and optionally prepare a neutral handover message.
Escalation_Condition: Always for a clearly unsupported MVP topic.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent a policy for an unsupported topic and do not ask the customer merely to rephrase a clearly out-of-scope request.
Acceptance_Criteria: The topic is correctly identified as outside MVP scope; no unsupported domain answer is generated; manual handling is indicated.

Input_or_Condition: Customer asks the assistant to perform or confirm a restricted action such as cancellation, order modification, customer-data change or a financial action.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Business Rules
Expected_Response_Behavior: Prepare only a safe handover or explanatory draft; keep the actual decision/action with a human.
Escalation_Condition: Always when execution of a restricted action is required.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not execute, confirm, simulate completion of or falsely claim success for a restricted action.
Acceptance_Criteria: No restricted action is performed or falsely confirmed; the request is routed to human handling.

Input_or_Condition: The request is in scope, but the required approved policy cannot be found.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Knowledge Base
Expected_Response_Behavior: State that the available internal information is insufficient and route the case for human review.
Escalation_Condition: Always when a required policy is unavailable.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not fill the knowledge gap from general knowledge or invented rules.
Acceptance_Criteria: No unsupported policy claim is generated; missing knowledge is explicit; escalation is triggered.

Input_or_Condition: Two or more retrieved internal rules conflict on a fact needed to answer the request.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Knowledge Base
Expected_Response_Behavior: Expose the conflict to the agent and route the case for manual resolution.
Escalation_Condition: Always when the contradiction affects the answer.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not silently choose one rule without an approved precedence rule.
Acceptance_Criteria: The contradiction is detected or surfaced; no definitive unsupported answer is produced; escalation occurs.

Input_or_Condition: An in-scope request requires OMS data, but the OMS lookup fails, times out or is unavailable.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Do not generate operational claims; tell the agent that required order data could not be retrieved and use a safe handover/retry path.
Escalation_Condition: Always when required operational data cannot be obtained reliably.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not infer order facts from the customer's statement alone.
Acceptance_Criteria: No order fact is invented; operational data unavailability is visible; safe fallback is used.

Input_or_Condition: The source responds, but a field necessary for a reliable decision is null, missing or unusable.
Required_Data: The missing field plus all other available use-case data.
Required_Sources: Order Management System and/or Knowledge Base
Expected_Response_Behavior: Ask for clarification only if the missing information can reasonably be supplied by the customer; otherwise route to human review.
Clarification_Condition: Missing information can be supplied reliably by the customer.
Escalation_Condition: Missing information is internal, cannot be customer-supplied, or is required for a business-critical decision.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not pretend that a missing internal field has a value.
Acceptance_Criteria: The action distinguishes customer-resolvable missing input from internal data gaps; no missing fact is fabricated.

Input_or_Condition: The system generates an answer using policy and/or operational data.
Required_Data: Business source identifiers and the content/facts used.
Required_Sources: Knowledge Base; Order Management System as applicable
Expected_Response_Behavior: Show human-readable business sources supporting the answer, for example policy section and order-data source.
Escalation_Condition: Use the escalation rule of the underlying use case.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not expose unnecessary technical prompt details as a substitute for business-source transparency.
Acceptance_Criteria: Displayed sources correspond to information actually used and support the generated answer.

Scenario_Name: Order shipped with ETA and tracking
Input_or_Condition: Order is uniquely identified; shipment_status=shipped; estimated_delivery_date and tracking_number are available.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Report verified shipment status, ETA and tracking information in the customer's language.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent carrier events or a more precise delivery time than OMS provides.
Acceptance_Criteria: Correct order is used; status/ETA/tracking match OMS; response is concise; OMS is shown as a source.

Input_or_Condition: Order is uniquely identified; shipment_status=processing; no shipment tracking exists yet.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain that the order is still being processed and report only available timing information.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent a tracking number or claim the order has shipped.
Acceptance_Criteria: Response matches OMS status; unavailable tracking is not fabricated; available ETA is represented correctly.

Input_or_Condition: Order is uniquely identified; shipment_status=delivered; delivered_at is available.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Report the verified delivered status and delivery timestamp/date.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not infer that the customer personally received the parcel.
Acceptance_Criteria: Delivered status and date match OMS; wording distinguishes system delivery status from customer confirmation.

Input_or_Condition: Customer asks for order status but no order can be uniquely identified.
Required_Sources: Customer Request
Expected_Response_Behavior: Ask for the order information required to identify the order.
Clarification_Condition: Always while no order can be uniquely identified.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate if identification remains impossible or manual identity verification is needed.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not guess an order from incomplete context.
Acceptance_Criteria: No order status is generated; clarification asks for a useful identifier.

Scenario_Name: Order ID provided but order not found
Input_or_Condition: Customer supplies an order ID, but OMS returns no matching order.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Allow correction of a likely mistyped identifier; if the identifier is confirmed and still not found, route to human review.
Clarification_Condition: The identifier may be incomplete or mistyped.
Escalation_Condition: Confirmed identifier still has no matching order.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not fabricate an order or state that it is cancelled/shipped/etc.
Acceptance_Criteria: No nonexistent order data is generated; the flow supports correction first and safe handover if unresolved.

Input_or_Condition: Order is identifiable and shipment status/ETA are available, but tracking_number is null.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Answer using the available verified status and ETA; omit or explicitly note unavailable tracking information.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent a tracking number.
Acceptance_Criteria: Known order facts are correct; missing tracking data is not fabricated; answer remains useful.

Scenario_Name: Customer thinks order is late but ETA is still in the future
Input_or_Condition: Customer reports a delay, but OMS estimated_delivery_date has not yet passed.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; estimated_delivery_date; current_date; shipping rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the verified ETA and applicable standard delivery expectation without treating the shipment as overdue.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not confirm a delay that is not supported by OMS and policy.
Acceptance_Criteria: Response reflects current date versus ETA correctly; shipping rule is applied; no unsupported delay claim is made.

Scenario_Name: ETA passed but still within policy grace period
Input_or_Condition: estimated_delivery_date has passed, but the delay is still within the policy-defined waiting/grace period.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; estimated_delivery_date; current_date; shipping rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Acknowledge the delay and explain the next step/timeframe defined by Shipping Policy.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not promise an investigation, refund or compensation before policy conditions are met.
Acceptance_Criteria: Delay calculation and next step match policy; response is grounded in OMS and Shipping Policy.

Input_or_Condition: The shipment delay meets the policy condition for further investigation or mandatory escalation.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; estimated_delivery_date; current_date; escalation rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Prepare a grounded response and clearly flag that the case requires further investigation by support.
Escalation_Condition: Policy investigation/escalation threshold is met.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not claim that investigation, replacement or refund has already been performed.
Acceptance_Criteria: Correct threshold is applied; action is ESCALATE; response does not promise an unsupported outcome.

Scenario_Name: ETA missing for a delay question
Input_or_Condition: Order exists, but estimated_delivery_date is missing and the policy decision depends on it.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: State that the required operational timing information is unavailable and route for human review.
Escalation_Condition: ETA is required to apply the delay rule and cannot be obtained.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not calculate or invent an expected date.
Acceptance_Criteria: Missing ETA is explicit; no invented date or delay threshold is used; escalation occurs.

Scenario_Name: Delivered status but customer reports missing parcel
Input_or_Condition: OMS shipment_status=delivered and customer states the parcel was not received.
Required_Data: order_id; shipment_status; delivered_at; relevant shipping rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Acknowledge the discrepancy, provide a safe draft and flag the case for investigation.
Escalation_Condition: Always under the current business rule.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not accuse the customer of receiving the parcel; do not initiate refund/replacement.
Acceptance_Criteria: Action is ESCALATE; OMS status is represented accurately; customer claim is not overwritten; source rule is shown.

Scenario_Name: Customer says delivered but OMS does not
Input_or_Condition: Customer refers to a delivered status, but OMS shows a non-delivered status.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy if needed
Expected_Response_Behavior: Use OMS as the authoritative operational source, explain the verified status, and escalate if the discrepancy cannot be resolved safely.
Escalation_Condition: The discrepancy affects the next action and cannot be resolved from approved sources.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not treat the customer's statement as authoritative operational data and do not hide the discrepancy.
Acceptance_Criteria: OMS facts are used; conflicting customer statement is handled carefully; no unsupported delivered claim is made.

Input_or_Condition: OMS reports shipment_status=delivered but delivered_at is missing.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Shipping Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Treat the internal data as incomplete and route the case for human review.
Escalation_Condition: Required delivery evidence is internally inconsistent/incomplete.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent the delivery date.
Acceptance_Criteria: Data inconsistency is visible; no fabricated timestamp is produced; escalation occurs.

Input_or_Condition: Order/item are identifiable; delivered_at is known; Returns Policy explicitly allows the return under the known conditions.
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; applicable return rules
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain that the known conditions satisfy the standard return policy and provide the relevant rule.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not imply that the return has already been initiated or approved beyond what policy supports.
Acceptance_Criteria: Eligibility conclusion matches policy and order/item facts; sources are shown; no extra exception is invented.

Input_or_Condition: Returns Policy clearly excludes the return under the known order/item conditions.
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; applicable exclusion rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the applicable exclusion or failed condition accurately and concisely.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not invent an exception or promise manual approval.
Acceptance_Criteria: Non-eligibility is supported by policy and facts; reason is clear; sources are shown.

Input_or_Condition: The return period calculated from delivered_at has expired and policy gives a clear standard rule.
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; current_date; items; return-period rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain that the standard return period has expired and state the approved rule.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate only if the customer requests an exception or policy requires discretionary review.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not grant an exception automatically.
Acceptance_Criteria: Return-period calculation is correct; standard rule is explained; no discretionary exception is invented.

Scenario_Name: Customer requests exception to return policy
Input_or_Condition: The standard policy does not allow the return, but the customer asks for an exception.
Required_Data: order_id; delivered_at; items; standard policy; exception rule if any
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy; Business Rules
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the standard rule and indicate that an exception requires human review unless an explicit approved exception rule applies.
Escalation_Condition: Human discretion is required.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not grant a discretionary exception.
Acceptance_Criteria: Standard policy is stated correctly; action is ESCALATE when discretion is needed; no unauthorized exception is promised.

Input_or_Condition: The order contains multiple items or the request does not identify which item the customer wants to return.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System
Expected_Response_Behavior: Ask which item the customer means before applying item-specific return rules.
Clarification_Condition: Always when item identity is necessary and ambiguous.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not choose an item arbitrarily.
Acceptance_Criteria: No eligibility conclusion is produced before the relevant item is identified; clarification is specific.

Input_or_Condition: Order/item are known, but the Returns Policy has no reliable rule for that product/category.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: State that the policy does not provide enough information for a reliable eligibility decision and route to human review.
Escalation_Condition: Policy coverage is insufficient for the item/category.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not generalize a return rule from unrelated categories.
Acceptance_Criteria: No unsupported eligibility claim is made; policy gap is explicit; escalation occurs.

Input_or_Condition: Customer asks how to return an item and the approved Returns Policy contains a general procedure.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Provide concise approved return steps in the customer's language.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not add steps, addresses, deadlines or labels not present in the approved policy.
Acceptance_Criteria: Procedure matches Returns Policy; no unnecessary OMS lookup is required; source is shown.

Input_or_Condition: The return process varies by item/category/order and the customer identifies a specific order.
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Returns Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Use the applicable item-specific procedure when policy covers it; otherwise route for human review.
Clarification_Condition: Clarify when the relevant item cannot be identified.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate when no approved procedure exists for the item/category.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not apply the generic process when policy explicitly defines a different process.
Acceptance_Criteria: Correct procedure variant is selected from policy and order data; unsupported variants are not invented.

Input_or_Condition: Order is identifiable and approved policy plus available order facts clearly support or reject standard refund eligibility.
Required_Data: order_id; relevant order facts; items; delivered_at if relevant; refund rules
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Refund Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the applicable refund eligibility rule and known facts without executing or promising a refund.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate if the decision requires discretion or unavailable data.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not issue, confirm or promise the refund.
Acceptance_Criteria: Eligibility explanation is grounded in policy and OMS; no refund action is claimed; sources are shown.

Scenario_Name: Customer asks support to issue refund now
Input_or_Condition: Customer explicitly requests that a refund be performed.
Required_Data: order_id; relevant order facts; refund policy; restricted-action rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Refund Policy; Business Rules
Expected_Response_Behavior: Prepare a policy-grounded draft for the agent and flag that actual refund decision/execution requires human handling.
Escalation_Condition: Always when an actual refund action is requested.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not say that the refund was initiated, approved or completed.
Acceptance_Criteria: Action is ESCALATE; no financial action is executed or falsely confirmed; useful policy context is still provided.

Scenario_Name: Known OMS fields insufficient for refund decision
Input_or_Condition: Refund Policy requires information not available in the current OMS data model, for example refund state or another eligibility fact.
Required_Data: order_id; available order facts; missing required eligibility field; refund rule
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Refund Policy
Expected_Response_Behavior: Identify the missing decision-relevant information and route the case for human review.
Escalation_Condition: Required internal eligibility information is unavailable.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not infer missing refund-state or eligibility facts.
Acceptance_Criteria: Missing data is explicit; no unsupported eligibility conclusion is generated; escalation occurs.

Input_or_Condition: Standard policy does not clearly permit the refund, but the customer asks for an exception.
Required_Data: order_id; relevant order facts; standard refund policy; exception rules if any
Required_Sources: Customer Request; Order Management System; Refund Policy; Business Rules
Expected_Response_Behavior: Explain the standard policy and keep the exception decision with a human unless an explicit approved rule resolves it.
Escalation_Condition: Human discretion is required.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not grant or promise an exception.
Acceptance_Criteria: Standard policy is represented accurately; action is ESCALATE when discretion is required; no unauthorized promise is made.

Input_or_Condition: Customer asks about a refund but no order can be uniquely identified and order-specific facts are required.
Required_Sources: Customer Request
Expected_Response_Behavior: Ask for the information required to identify the relevant order.
Clarification_Condition: Always when order-specific refund evaluation is required but the order is unknown.
Escalation_Condition: Escalate if the order cannot be identified after clarification or manual verification is required.
Prohibited_Behavior: Do not evaluate refund eligibility for an unknown order.
Acceptance_Criteria: No eligibility claim is generated; clarification is targeted; safe handover is available if unresolved.
